entities.summary: Elizabethan playhouse (built 1599) in Southwark, London, associated with William Shakespeare and the Lord Chamberlain's Men. The open-air amphitheater's design — standing pit, tiered galleries, thrust stage — created an intimate performance space where Shakespeare's plays reached audiences from groundlings to royalty, defining English dramatic tradition.
